subject: Re: Feature enablement — streaming + tool-calling schema alignment
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@pulseai.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: integrations@pulseai.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Feature enablement: streaming + toolcalling schema alignment

Hi Rachel / Monica —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. PulseAI is eager to move from PoC to a narrow production rollout for our "Live Assist" feature. Key asks we want to align on for the enablement sprint:

- Streaming responses with partial JSON outputs (we stream incremental JSON chunks back to the client).
- Tool/function calling for lookups (SaaS provisioning and ticket creation).
- A deterministic JSON schema for structured outputs so our front-end can hydrate UI components predictably.

I've attached an initial schema (pulse_schema_v1.json) and a short sample payload. Our timeline target: pilot in the San Francisco market by June 20.

Can Redwood confirm the following by EOD Thu:
1) Whether streaming partial JSON is supported with your runtime's current kernel selection (we saw demo that streamed text).
2) Guidance on best-practice for embedding tool-call metadata in the stream (to avoid corrupting JSON when partial tokens arrive).
3) A suggested mutual action plan / responsibilities matrix for the next three weeks.

If helpful, Tom Hayes from our infra team (copied) will coordinate a short tech call.

Thanks —
Jordan Ellis
Head of Integrations | PulseAI
jordan.ellis@pulseai.com
Attachments: pulse_schema_v1.json (application/json, 18KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@pulseai.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Feature enablement: streaming + toolcalling schema alignment

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear ask and timeline. Quick responses to your three bullets, plus a proposed MAP below.

1) Streaming partial JSON: supported. Redwood can stream structured tokens but we recommend a framing layer (boundary tokens) so the consumer can stitch partial objects reliably. We provide a small client helper that reassembles tokenized JSON safely.

2) Tool-call metadata: we suggest a side-channel metadata envelope per token (we call it "meta-span") rather than inline tool markers. That avoids breaking JSON and is compatible with our function-calling API. We'll share an example in the spec folder.

3) Mutual action plan: see the short MAP attached (enabling-mvp-playlist.xlsx). High level:
- Week 1: Schema finalization + ingestion test harness (PulseAI owns feature flags; Redwood owns runtime config and client helper).
- Week 2: Canary with 5% traffic, validate structured outputs + tool call success metrics.
- Week 3: Ops runbook and full roll to SF market.

I've looped in Laura (CS lead) for scheduling and Monica (solutions engineer) for the schema details. Proposed times for kickoff call: Thu 5/16 10:00am PT or Fri 5/17 11:00am PT — please confirm.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Manager, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Attachments: enabling-mvp-playlist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 42KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@pulseai.com>, rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Feature enablement: streaming + toolcalling schema alignment

Jordan / Rachel —

Tech follow-up from my side. Quick engineering notes and acceptance criteria we need to agree on before the canary: 

Acceptance criteria (engineering):
- JSON schema must specify optional "partial": true/false field so the stitcher knows if payload is incomplete.
- Tool-calls must be expressed as separate JSON objects with stable ids: {"tool_call":{"id":"uuid","name":"create_ticket","args":{...}}} and must be emitted on the metadata side-channel.
- A delivery guarantee matrix: what happens on partial window drop? Redwood will surface token-level retries and we will supply sample telemetry to validate.

Example framing we recommend (pseudocode):
--METAFRAME START--
{"meta":{"span_id":"s-12345","seq":1}}
--CHUNK--
{...partial json chunk...}
--METAFRAME END--

This keeps the runtime agnostic and preserves JSON integrity. I've uploaded the proposed framed examples to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-pulse-integration-specs

Operational ask: Dylan (cc) will own the canary instrumentation config on the Redwood side; please confirm the telemetry keys we should expect.

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@pulseai.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: t.hayes@cloudops.io, integrations@pulseai.com
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Feature enablement: streaming + toolcalling schema alignment

Thanks — that framing approach looks sensible and aligns with our front-end team's stitching logic. A couple of notes:

- We can add the optional partial flag on our side.
- Tool-call envelope with "id" and "args" is acceptable. We'll map Redwood telemetry keys to our monitoring.
- We accept the proposed MAP and can commit engineering resources for Week 1 tests.

One admin item: PulseAI legal needs the SOW signed (small amendment for tool-call telemetry). I've started a DocuSign envelope (link below). If we can get that signed by Fri 5/17, we'll be green for the pilot.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/ENVELOPEID/0a7c9

I'll confirm kickoff slot after the legal sign-off. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Jordan
